deck.section_name: 13. An Introduction to AS Level Organic Chemistry
deck.title: Shapes of Organic Molecules; σ & π Bonds

front_blocks.md: Define **straight-chain organic molecule**.

back_blocks.md: A **straight-chain organic molecule** is one in which all carbon atoms are connected to each other in one continuous, unbranched chain.

cards.front_md: Define **straight-chain organic molecule**.
cards.back_md: A **straight-chain organic molecule** is one in which all carbon atoms are connected to each other in one continuous, unbranched chain.

front_blocks.md: What distinguishes a branched organic molecule from a straight-chain molecule?

back_blocks.md: A **branched** organic molecule has one or more **side groups** (alkyl groups) attached to the main carbon chain, whereas a straight-chain molecule has no side branches.

cards.front_md: What distinguishes a branched organic molecule from a straight-chain molecule?
cards.back_md: A **branched** organic molecule has one or more **side groups** (alkyl groups) attached to the main carbon chain, whereas a straight-chain molecule has no side branches.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Cyclic organic compounds are always aromatic.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**Cyclic** organic molecules simply have carbon atoms connected in a ring. They are **aliphatic** unless they contain a **benzene ring**, which would make them aromatic.

cards.front_md:

cards.back_md:

**Cyclic** organic molecules simply have carbon atoms connected in a ring. They are **aliphatic** unless they contain a **benzene ring**, which would make them aromatic.

front_blocks.md: Define **cyclic organic molecule**.

back_blocks.md: A **cyclic organic molecule** is one in which the carbon atoms are connected to each other in a **ring** structure.

cards.front_md: Define **cyclic organic molecule**.
cards.back_md: A **cyclic organic molecule** is one in which the carbon atoms are connected to each other in a **ring** structure.

front_blocks.md: Straight, branched and cyclic organic molecules are all called **..........**  compounds, provided they do not contain a **..........**  ring.

back_blocks.md: Straight, branched and cyclic organic molecules are all called **aliphatic** compounds, provided they do not contain a **benzene** ring.

cards.front_md: Straight, branched and cyclic organic molecules are all called **..........**  compounds, provided they do not contain a **..........**  ring.
cards.back_md: Straight, branched and cyclic organic molecules are all called **aliphatic** compounds, provided they do not contain a **benzene** ring.

front_blocks.md: Give one example each of a straight-chain, a branched and a cyclic alkane.

back_blocks.md: Straight-chain: **butane** (C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>). Branched: **2-methylbutane** (C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>12</sub>). Cyclic: **cyclopentane** (C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>10</sub>).

cards.front_md: Give one example each of a straight-chain, a branched and a cyclic alkane.
cards.back_md: Straight-chain: **butane** (C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>). Branched: **2-methylbutane** (C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>12</sub>). Cyclic: **cyclopentane** (C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>10</sub>).

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
2-methylbutane is a straight-chain organic molecule.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**2-methylbutane** is a **branched** molecule: it has a four-carbon main chain with a methyl group attached at carbon 2.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

2-methylbutane is a straight-chain organic molecule.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

**2-methylbutane** is a **branched** molecule: it has a four-carbon main chain with a methyl group attached at carbon 2.

front_blocks.md: In a branched molecule, the side groups are attached to the **..........**  chain. In a cyclic molecule, carbons are connected in a **..........**  shape.

back_blocks.md: In a branched molecule, the side groups are attached to the **main** chain. In a cyclic molecule, carbons are connected in a **ring** shape.

cards.front_md: In a branched molecule, the side groups are attached to the **..........**  chain. In a cyclic molecule, carbons are connected in a **..........**  shape.
cards.back_md: In a branched molecule, the side groups are attached to the **main** chain. In a cyclic molecule, carbons are connected in a **ring** shape.

front_blocks.md: What three structural arrangements can the carbon atoms take in aliphatic organic compounds?

back_blocks.md: Carbon atoms in aliphatic compounds can be arranged as **straight chains**, **branched chains** or **cyclic rings** (provided no benzene ring is present).

cards.front_md: What three structural arrangements can the carbon atoms take in aliphatic organic compounds?
cards.back_md: Carbon atoms in aliphatic compounds can be arranged as **straight chains**, **branched chains** or **cyclic rings** (provided no benzene ring is present).

front_blocks.md: Define **sigma (σ) bond**.

back_blocks.md: A **sigma bond** is formed by the **end-on overlap** of atomic orbitals. Electron density is symmetrical about the line joining the two nuclei.

cards.front_md: Define **sigma (σ) bond**.
cards.back_md: A **sigma bond** is formed by the **end-on overlap** of atomic orbitals. Electron density is symmetrical about the line joining the two nuclei.

front_blocks.md: What hybridisation state does a carbon atom have when it forms four sigma bonds, and what shape does this produce?

back_blocks.md: A carbon forming four σ bonds is **sp**<sup>**3**</sup>** hybridised**, giving a **tetrahedral** arrangement with bond angles of **109.5°**.

cards.front_md: What hybridisation state does a carbon atom have when it forms four sigma bonds, and what shape does this produce?
cards.back_md: A carbon forming four σ bonds is **sp**<sup>**3**</sup>** hybridised**, giving a **tetrahedral** arrangement with bond angles of **109.5°**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A double bond consists of one sigma bond and one pi bond.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
A **double bond** is made up of one **σ bond** (end-on orbital overlap) and one **π bond** (sideways p orbital overlap).

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A double bond consists of one sigma bond and one pi bond.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

A **double bond** is made up of one **σ bond** (end-on orbital overlap) and one **π bond** (sideways p orbital overlap).

front_blocks.md: Define **pi (π) bond**.

back_blocks.md: A **pi bond** is formed by the **sideways overlap** of p orbitals. The two electron clouds lie above and below (or in front of and behind) the plane of the bonded atoms.

cards.front_md: Define **pi (π) bond**.
cards.back_md: A **pi bond** is formed by the **sideways overlap** of p orbitals. The two electron clouds lie above and below (or in front of and behind) the plane of the bonded atoms.

front_blocks.md: An sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon forms **..........**  sigma bonds and has **..........**  p orbital(s) left for sideways overlap, resulting in **..........**  pi bond(s) per carbon–carbon double bond.

back_blocks.md: An sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon forms **three** sigma bonds and has **one** p orbital(s) left for sideways overlap, resulting in **one** pi bond(s) per carbon–carbon double bond.

cards.front_md: An sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon forms **..........**  sigma bonds and has **..........**  p orbital(s) left for sideways overlap, resulting in **..........**  pi bond(s) per carbon–carbon double bond.
cards.back_md: An sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon forms **three** sigma bonds and has **one** p orbital(s) left for sideways overlap, resulting in **one** pi bond(s) per carbon–carbon double bond.

front_blocks.md: What hybridisation state is present in ethyne and what bond angle does it produce?

back_blocks.md: The carbon atoms in ethyne are **sp hybridised**, giving a **linear** arrangement with bond angles of **180°**.

cards.front_md: What hybridisation state is present in ethyne and what bond angle does it produce?
cards.back_md: The carbon atoms in ethyne are **sp hybridised**, giving a **linear** arrangement with bond angles of **180°**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A triple bond consists of one sigma bond and two pi bonds.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
A **triple bond** contains one **σ bond** and two **π bonds**, formed from the end-on overlap of one orbital pair and the sideways overlap of two pairs of p orbitals.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A triple bond consists of one sigma bond and two pi bonds.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

A **triple bond** contains one **σ bond** and two **π bonds**, formed from the end-on overlap of one orbital pair and the sideways overlap of two pairs of p orbitals.

front_blocks.md: sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon atoms adopt a **..........**  arrangement with bond angles of **..........**. sp<sup>3</sup> hybridised carbon atoms adopt a **..........**  arrangement with bond angles of 109.5°.

back_blocks.md: sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon atoms adopt a **planar** arrangement with bond angles of **120°**. sp<sup>3</sup> hybridised carbon atoms adopt a **tetrahedral** arrangement with bond angles of 109.5°.

cards.front_md: sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon atoms adopt a **..........**  arrangement with bond angles of **..........**. sp<sup>3</sup> hybridised carbon atoms adopt a **..........**  arrangement with bond angles of 109.5°.
cards.back_md: sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon atoms adopt a **planar** arrangement with bond angles of **120°**. sp<sup>3</sup> hybridised carbon atoms adopt a **tetrahedral** arrangement with bond angles of 109.5°.

front_blocks.md: Why does bond strength increase from single to double to triple bonds?

back_blocks.md: Each additional bond increases the **electron density** between the carbon atoms, making the bond **stronger** and harder to break. Bond strength order: single < double < triple.

cards.front_md: Why does bond strength increase from single to double to triple bonds?
cards.back_md: Each additional bond increases the **electron density** between the carbon atoms, making the bond **stronger** and harder to break. Bond strength order: single < double < triple.

front_blocks.md: Define **planar molecule**.

back_blocks.md: A **planar molecule** is one in which all atoms lie in the same plane.

cards.front_md: Define **planar molecule**.
cards.back_md: A **planar molecule** is one in which all atoms lie in the same plane.

front_blocks.md: Why does the presence of an sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon force a molecule to adopt a trigonal planar shape?

back_blocks.md: An sp<sup>2</sup> carbon has three σ bonds that spread into a **trigonal planar** arrangement (120° bond angles) to **minimise repulsion** between bonding pairs of electrons.

cards.front_md: Why does the presence of an sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon force a molecule to adopt a trigonal planar shape?
cards.back_md: An sp<sup>2</sup> carbon has three σ bonds that spread into a **trigonal planar** arrangement (120° bond angles) to **minimise repulsion** between bonding pairs of electrons.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Ethene is a planar molecule.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Ethene has two sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbons, each forming a **trigonal planar** centre. All six atoms lie in the same plane.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Ethene is a planar molecule.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

Ethene has two sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbons, each forming a **trigonal planar** centre. All six atoms lie in the same plane.

front_blocks.md: sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon gives a **..........**  planar shape with bond angles of **..........**. sp hybridised carbon gives a **..........**  shape with bond angles of 180°.

back_blocks.md: sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon gives a **trigonal** planar shape with bond angles of **120°**. sp hybridised carbon gives a **linear** shape with bond angles of 180°.

cards.front_md: sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon gives a **..........**  planar shape with bond angles of **..........**. sp hybridised carbon gives a **..........**  shape with bond angles of 180°.
cards.back_md: sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon gives a **trigonal** planar shape with bond angles of **120°**. sp hybridised carbon gives a **linear** shape with bond angles of 180°.

front_blocks.md: Propene has one sp<sup>3</sup> centre and two sp<sup>2</sup> centres. Which part of the molecule is planar and which is not?

back_blocks.md: The two carbons of the **C=C double bond** and all atoms directly bonded to them are in the same plane (trigonal planar centres). The **CH**<sub>**3**</sub> group is **tetrahedral** and not part of the planar region.

cards.front_md: Propene has one sp<sup>3</sup> centre and two sp<sup>2</sup> centres. Which part of the molecule is planar and which is not?
cards.back_md: The two carbons of the **C=C double bond** and all atoms directly bonded to them are in the same plane (trigonal planar centres). The **CH**<sub>**3**</sub> group is **tetrahedral** and not part of the planar region.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Ethyne is a non-planar molecule.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Ethyne is a **linear** (and therefore planar) molecule. Its two sp hybridised carbons arrange their σ bonds at 180° to minimise repulsion.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Ethyne is a non-planar molecule.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Ethyne is a **linear** (and therefore planar) molecule. Its two sp hybridised carbons arrange their σ bonds at 180° to minimise repulsion.

front_blocks.md: Propyne has one **..........**  centre (from the C–C triple bond region) and one **..........**  centre (from the CH<sub>3</sub> group).

back_blocks.md: Propyne has one **linear** centre (from the C–C triple bond region) and one **tetrahedral** centre (from the CH<sub>3</sub> group).

cards.front_md: Propyne has one **..........**  centre (from the C–C triple bond region) and one **..........**  centre (from the CH<sub>3</sub> group).
cards.back_md: Propyne has one **linear** centre (from the C–C triple bond region) and one **tetrahedral** centre (from the CH<sub>3</sub> group).

front_blocks.md: Define **trigonal planar arrangement**.

back_blocks.md: A **trigonal planar arrangement** is a molecular geometry in which three groups around a central atom lie in the same plane at bond angles of **120°**, as seen in sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbons.

cards.front_md: Define **trigonal planar arrangement**.
cards.back_md: A **trigonal planar arrangement** is a molecular geometry in which three groups around a central atom lie in the same plane at bond angles of **120°**, as seen in sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbons.

front_blocks.md: Give two examples of planar molecular shapes and state a bond angle for each.

back_blocks.md: Examples: **trigonal planar** (120°, e.g. ethene) and **linear** (180°, e.g. ethyne). Both have all atoms in the same plane.
